title: Marable band personnel
summary: Kimball lists the men on the boat band: Campbell, Marable, Humphrey, Story, Dewey Jackson, Irvin Randolph.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: Can you remember almost everybody else?

Yes, I can remember almost all of the fellas there. We had Floyd Campbell, he was playing drums. Faith Marable playing piano. Tom Lovingood playing piano. My father was playing bass, violin, and the sousaphone. Willie Humphrey was playing clarinet and tenor sax. Bert, oh, what's Bert's name?

He played saxophone, alto saxophone and baritone. And his brother-in-law played alto saxophone and baritone. They had three sax, and Nathaniel Story played trombone. Oh yeah. Dewey Jackson played trumpet. And, any other trumpets? I'm trying to think of other trumpets. First, second trumpet. Oh, Irvin Randolph. Oh yeah. Irvin Randolph. Yeah, I knew him in Chicago, yeah. Yes.
He worked with Louis Armstrong up there. That's right.
Irvin Randolph. He played second trumpet. That was just about the lineup then. I was playing banjo then. And, uh, Floyd Campbell sang beautifully. He had a very nice voice.
And he made some records with Charlie Creff I believe.
